component_findings.abstraction_reuse: Recertified level 4 under the current criterion: Functions, modules/types and generic/polymorphic abstraction support reusable composition across ordinary programs. Evidence basis: Qualitative structural review of Rust language surface using template/programs/rust/adversarial and template/programs/rust/micro reference programs (ADV-01..ADV-26, mb00..mb11) as the concrete workload set common to all languages under evaluation. | Rust supports algebraic data types (enums with payload variants), pattern matching with exhaustiveness checking, trait-based polymorphism (static and dynamic dispatch via dyn Trait), generics with trait bounds, closures with capture-by-move/borrow, RAII-based resource management, zero-cost abstractions (iterators compiling to loops), and a strong ownership/borrowing model expressed directly in the type system (e.g. ADV-01_R.rs shows explicit narrowing-cast semantics `as i32`, ADV-06/07/08 exercise trait objects and lifetime-sensitive constructs typical of the adversarial suite). | Micro-benchmark programs (mb01-mb11) exercise numeric, collection, string, and control-flow idioms showing the language expresses common workload patterns (loops, recursion, vectors, hashmaps, iterators, error propagation via Result/Option and the `?` operator) concisely without external libraries. | Compared to C/C-like baselines (ADV-*_C.rs vs ADV-*_R.rs pairs), the Rust variants (_R) require explicit, safe input handling (e.g. read_line + parse::<i64>) rather than implicit unchecked conversions, illustrating higher expressiveness of safety-relevant inte…
